title: Zygote, Forking, and Application Process Creation

scout.purpose: Understand zygote, forking, and application process creation as a causal Android engineering system rather than a vocabulary item.
scout.realWorldUse: Expert Android diagnosis requires tracing responsibility through processes, framework services, threads, queues, graphics buffers, and system composition.
scout.outcome: You can explain, inspect, test, and safely apply zygote, forking, and application process creation.

blocks.text: During boot, init starts Zygote for the relevant ABI. Zygote preloads runtime classes and resources, starts ART infrastructure, and listens for process-start requests. Forking gives a child a copy-on-write view of prepared memory, reducing startup work and sharing clean pages. Modern systems may use unspecialised app process pools when configured, but the conceptual boundary remains: a generic child is specialised with UID, GID, capabilities, SELinux context, runtime flags, package data, and an application entry point.

blocks.text: A request from system_server reaches Zygote through its command socket after ActivityManager determines a process is needed. The child must not inherit dangerous open descriptors or privileged state; Zygote enforces file-descriptor hygiene and sets credentials before application code runs. The app child invokes the runtime entry that leads to ActivityThread.main, creates the main Looper, attaches to system services through Binder, and waits for scheduled components. Forking does not clone another app process or its live objects.

blocks.text: Trace a cold launch using Perfetto process-start events, logcat activity manager messages, ps parent relationships, and AOSP source. Distinguish time before fork, specialisation, runtime bind, provider and Application initialization, activity launch, and first frame. Device releases, ABI, USAP configuration, profiles, page size, storage, and thermal state can alter timings. Never design app correctness around implementation details such as exact preloaded classes or a stable Zygote PID; public lifecycle and persistence contracts remain authoritative.

Platform internals are a causal map for diagnosis, not an invitation to depend on hidden APIs. Trace ownership across process, thread, Binder, token, queue, buffer, and display boundaries; distinguish public contracts from release-specific implementation. Use AOSP source matching the device branch, Perfetto, dumpsys, logcat, bug reports, and controlled experiments as complementary evidence. Record Android build, device, configuration, process state, workload, and timestamps. Test death, cancellation, reentrancy, backpressure, configuration, multi-window, and resource pressure. When a private class or trace label changes, the explanation should still stand at the responsibility level. Production apps use supported APIs, while platform changes require compatibility tests, security policy, boot and performance evidence, and safe rollback.

blocks.title: Common systems trap
blocks.text: Watch carefully for this common failure mode in production: Describing Zygote as a template containing a fully initialized copy of each app incorrectly implies that application objects and user state exist before the fork.

trap_check.mistake: Describing Zygote as a template containing a fully initialized copy of each app incorrectly implies that application objects and user state exist before the fork.
trap_check.why: It collapses distinct ownership or timing boundaries and can produce a confident but incorrect diagnosis.
trap_check.fix: Trace the complete causal path with matching source and runtime evidence before changing the system.

trap_check.mistake: Depending on a hidden API, internal class name, trace label, or one device observation as a stable application contract.
trap_check.why: Platform implementation and vendor behavior can change while public compatibility guarantees remain different.
trap_check.fix: Use internals for explanation and diagnosis, but implement app behavior through supported APIs and test across versions.

recall.prompt: Why does Zygote preload common runtime state?
recall.answer: Forked children can reuse clean copy-on-write pages and avoid repeating part of runtime initialization.

recall.prompt: What must be recorded with systems evidence?
recall.answer: The Android and app build, device, configuration, starting state, workload, process or thread context, and exact capture method.

recall.prompt: How should application code use platform-internals knowledge?
recall.answer: Use it to diagnose and reason about public behavior, not to depend on hidden implementation APIs or names.
